what_its_for: Rizatriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults and children 6 years and older. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with migraines. It is NOT used to prevent migraines or to treat other types of headaches like tension headaches.
how_to_take: Take rizatriptan as soon as you feel a migraine coming on. You can take the regular tablet with or without food and swallow it whole with water. If you have the orally disintegrating tablet (Maxalt-MLT), open the foil pouch with dry hands, place the tablet on your tongue, and let it dissolve completely — do not chew or swallow it whole. The dissolved tablet can be swallowed with or without water. If your headache comes back after the first dose, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first. Do NOT take more than 30 mg in a 24-hour period.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 5 mg or 10 mg taken at the start of a migraine. If the headache returns, a second dose may be taken at least 2 hours later. Do not take more than 30 mg in one day. For children 6 to 17 years old, the dose is based on weight and will be determined by the doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Rizatriptan is taken only when you have a migraine, not on a regular daily schedule. There is no 'missed dose' to worry about. Simply take it when your next migraine starts. Never take a double dose to make up for one you skipped.
storage: Store rizatriptan at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep the orally disintegrating tablets (Maxalt-MLT) in their original foil pouches until you are ready to use them. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking rizatriptan if you have already taken another triptan medication (like sumatriptan or zolmitriptan) or an ergotamine-type drug (like Cafergot) within the last 24 hours. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how rizatriptan affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, as it can worsen side effects. Do not use rizatriptan to treat more than 10 headache days per month, as this can lead to medication-overuse headaches.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; shortness of breath; severe stomach pain; sudden severe headache different from your usual migraines; weakness or numbness on one side of the body; slurred speech; vision changes; fast or pounding heartbeat; skin rash or hives; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; or signs of serotonin syndrome such as agitation, hallucinations, fever, sweating, muscle twitching, or diarrhea. Also contact your doctor if your migraines are not getting better or if you are taking rizatriptan more than 10 days per month.
when_it_works: Rizatriptan usually starts working within 30 minutes to 2 hours after you take it. Many people feel significant relief within 2 hours. Results can vary from person to person.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using rizatriptan if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose if you have kidney or liver problems. Older adults (65+): Use with caution; your doctor will determine if this medication is safe for you. Children under 6 years: Rizatriptan is not approved for use in children under 6 years old. People with heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or a history of stroke should NOT use rizatriptan. Always inform your doctor of all medical conditions and medications you are taking, including supplements.
